The most realistic hacking sim I've played. It has a similar style to Uplink but more command-line based, which I really enjoy more than the visual UI of Uplink. That said, outside of the (amazing) storyline and meticulously-placed references to tech and hacking culture, there's not a lot of gameplay depth. There aren't upgrades to look forward to or a working ranking system (you will always be rank 0), so you're here for the experience more than progression. This is much more of a puzzle game, and a very enjoyable one at that. If the game looks at all interested, I would highly recommend it.

Awesome game, finished it in one looongg sitting. 

For one, I don't think this is meant to be an authentic or accurate hacking experience, but it does a great job of simulating one for the player. It doesn't take a whole lot to get it down, but it also isn't so easy that it gets boring later on. It keeps it challenging even toward the end and the solutions aren't spoonfed. It can get your head scratching at times, but that's part of the fun of figuring it out for yourself. It's got a good story and I like how it's up to the player to explore little bits and pieces of it scattered all over. I also like how it isn't 100% linear, with the options to change themes, not to pursue certain parts, and the number of solutions. Everyone can have different experiences and it does a lot for mainly being a "terminal / hacking game"

Definitely pick this up if you're into these types of games, really worth it especially on sale. 

Also, upon playing the Labyrinths DLC after the base game, I found that to be an amazing experience as well. I would even go as far as saying that I liked that storyline more. Snag it up, especially in a sale, even if you already finished the base game. I found that it was a bit more challenging than the midsection (where it would normally pop up when playing for the first time) and the storyline was more impactful.

I'm sure it gets compared to Uplink all the time, but it truly is just a much better Uplink with a lot of the 2001-era cruft removed.

I really appreciate the use of actual linux commands, although tbh as someone who uses linux on a day-to-day basis, I do feel like they could have added more functionality. For example, if one wants to run more than one coomand at a time they could use command one && command two. Idk if this was not included for balance reasons, but it would be useful if it was added. Also, most distros come with some sort of text editor, usually, vim, nano or emacs. I usually use one of those if I need to edit a file in the terminal. I was also disappointed that hidden files weren't implemented. It would have been interesting if this was implemented if for no other reason than realism. Hidden files and directories are a thing on pretty much every system (basically so you don't get program folders listed when you are just manipulating routine files and whatnot. Despite my nitpicking, I did enjoy the game and I do think this game would be a nice intro to the linux command line for those interested in that (although spoiler alert: most of us use the graphical interface most of the time lol). Just know that there is a lot of stuff left out for simplicity's sake.

What a rush. There's tons of detail crammed into this game, and it manages to create feeling of both pressure and intense curiosity at every turn. Don't worry if you aren't cmd / linux literate, the game will guide you so that you have all the tools you'll need for every task, you just need to bring your brain. For the price it's at, 110% worth it.

Easily one of my favorite games of all time. The terminal isn't 100% a Linux/Unix terminal, but the fact that it operates almost exactly like one (albeit with only a few commands), coupled with the impressive and actually somewhat customizable UI, the fun characters and missions, and the immersive plot, makes this a game I can't recommend enough for both cybersecurity/ethical hacking nerds like myself and even casual players with an interest in hacking. It's not completely realistic, and it doesn't need to be. The lengths the game went to are MORE than enough for me.
